page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.16xlarge is an x86_64 architecture instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 256 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps.

Multi-core benchmark results place this instance in the top 25% tier, as demonstrated by strong scores in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, and stress-ng multi-core tests. It also exhibits strong performance in Passmark database operations and LLM inference for small 135M models. Conversely, single-core performance metrics, including stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the average middle 50% range. Memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput also align with average tier performance.

The lack of local storage requires reliance on external block storage, which may impact I/O-intensive workloads. However, the high vCPU count and strong multi-core scaling make it suitable for parallel processing tasks, software compilation, database operations, and medium-scale LLM inference. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is defined by its high resource density and balanced CPU-to-memory ratio, offering a stable environment for enterprise applications that do not require local NVMe drives or GPU acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-hypervised instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, placing it in the top 25% for multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and software compilation. However, single-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth remain in the average middle 50% tier. With a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps, this instance is suited for parallel processing, database management, and enterprise applications that utilize network-attached storage.
